newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ninety-thousand Turks in grandstand job contest.
newsitem.headline: Ninety-thousand Turks in grandstand job contest.

text.p: Around 90,000 people have applied for just 2,500 unskilled jobs in Turkey's social security institution, Employment Minister Necati Celik told a news conference on Monday.
The new personnel are to be selected through an examination held in two football stadiums Ankara on Thursday. The two- and-a-half hour examination will involve a staff of 3,100 supervisors.

Last week people travelled from all over Turkey to apply for the jobs. Many camped out for days in order to be in with a chance of one of the jobs, which pay an average of 18 million lira ($180) a month.

"If applictions had been accepted at a provincial level, the 90,000 aplications would have become 300,000. Disappointing these people and their families is most distressing. It was to avoid disappointing too many people that the applications were taken in Ankara," Celik said.

Celik blamed the high level of applications on widespread unemployment in Turkey. Unemployment in Turkey was officially 6.3 percent in April, the latest figure available, but unofficially it is estimated to be about 15 percent.
"If possible, I'm thinking of leaving not just Ankara, but the country, so as to avoid all the arguments," Celik said.
